parameter_stage_gibbs <- function(posterior_temp = posterior_temp,taxa.appear.core=taxa.appear.core,taxa_information=taxa_information){
    
    posterior_temp$parameter_ratio <- 1
    which_taxa <- rep(0,num_taxa)
    which_taxa[posterior_temp$z] <- 1
    # https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/44494/why-is-the-dirichlet-distribution-the-prior-for-the-multinomial-distribution
    # jeffreys prior (non-informative): prior$taxa.weights * prior$phi1
    testing <- F
    while (testing == F) {
        new_weight <- SBMSplitMerge::rdirichlet(1,posterior_temp$jeffreys_prior + which_taxa)
        if (min(new_weight) > 0) {
            testing <- T
        }
    }
    posterior_temp$taxa_weights <- new_weight   
    # gibbs: alpha
    # The uniform distribution is actually a special case of the Dirichlet distribution, corresponding to the case α1=α2=⋯=αk=1 or 0.5
#     alpha_unnorm <- new_weight * posterior_temp$taxa_weights[1,] # theta * Pr(P|A,z) ~ Unif(1,num_taxa)
#     alpha_unnorm <- alpha_unnorm/max(alpha_unnorm)
#     posterior_temp$alpha <- alpha_unnorm/sum(alpha_unnorm)

    posterior_temp$z <- SBMSplitMerge::rcat( posterior_temp$how_many_taxa,posterior_temp$taxa_weights,replace=FALSE)
    posterior_temp$combination[posterior_temp$z] <- 1
    # modify the taxa information: Pr(P|A,z,w)
    taxa.appear.core.temp <- taxa.appear.core[ , posterior_temp$z]
    posterior_temp$taxa.appear.core.temp <- taxa.appear.core.temp / rowSums(taxa.appear.core.temp, na.rm=T)
    
    posterior_temp$parameter_ratio <- 1
    
    return(posterior_temp)

}

parameter_stage_weights <- function(posterior_temp=posterior_temp,taxa.appear.core=taxa.appear.core,taxa_information=taxa_information){
    old_weights <- posterior_temp$taxa_weights
    testing <- F
    counts <- 0
    while (testing == F) {
        counts <- counts + 1
        new_weights <- rdirichlet(1,old_weights*posterior_temp$dirichlet_spread)[1,]  
        if (min(new_weights) > 0) {
            testing <- T
        }
        # start again, if the algorithm runs into a dead end
        if(counts >= 1000){
            new_weights <- rep(1/((num_taxa)),num_taxa)
            posterior_temp$dirichlet_spread <- posterior_temp$dirichlet_spread*2
            testing <- T
        }
    }
    posterior_temp$taxa_weights <- new_weights
    # parameter module
    # https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/64674/confused-with-mcmc-metropolis-hastings-variations-random-walk-non-random-walk
    # better: https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/64293/understanding-metropolis-hastings-with-asymmetric-proposal-distribution
#     weights_ratio <- ddirichlet(posterior_temp$taxa_weights,rep(0.5,num_taxa))/ddirichlet(posterior$taxa_weights[[i-1]],rep(0.5,num_taxa))
#     weights_ratio <- ddirichlet(new_weights,old_weights*posterior_temp$dirichlet_spread) / ddirichlet(old_weights,old_weights*posterior_temp$dirichlet_spread)
#     proposal_ratio <- ddirichlet(old_weights,new_weights*posterior_temp$dirichlet_spread)/ddirichlet(new_weights,old_weights*posterior_temp$dirichlet_spread)

    
    # dirichlet is not a symmetric distribution
    weights_ratio <- ddirichlet(new_weights,rep(0.5,num_taxa)) / ddirichlet(old_weights,rep(0.5,num_taxa))
    proposal_ratio <- ddirichlet(old_weights,new_weights)/ddirichlet(new_weights,old_weights)
    
    parameter_ratio <- proposal_ratio * weights_ratio
    if(is.na(parameter_ratio)) parameter_ratio <- 0
    posterior_temp$parameter_ratio <- parameter_ratio
    
    taxa.appear.core.temp <- matrix(taxa_information$values * new_weights,ncol = taxa_information$ncol_taxa_array,nrow=taxa_information$nrow_taxa_array,byrow=T)
    posterior_temp$taxa.appear.core.temp <- taxa.appear.core.temp / rowSums(taxa.appear.core.temp, na.rm=T)
    
    # default z values
    posterior_temp$z <- 1:ncol(taxa.appear.core.temp)
    
    return(posterior_temp)
}
